Following:
 Judgment

This intra-court appeal arises out of the impugned order 30th March 2022 passed in W.P.
No.101184/2022 whereby the said petition filed by the appellant was dismissed by the learned Single Judge.
2. The material on record discloses that there exists a tomb of the sixth pontiff of the appellant-Math for 600 years.

When a notice dated 03.08.2021 was issued by respondents No.1 to 3 calling upon the appellant to NC: 2023:KHC-D:10532-DB remove the tomb since it was situated on a Highway, the Shri. sentences.text: 2 appellant approached this Court in W.P. No.102746/2021.

During the course of hearing, by way of response to the contention of the appellant that there was certain divinity attached to the tomb of the sixth pontiff of the appellant- Math and that the tomb should not be disturbed or relocated and deviation can be made to the Highway instead of removing or relocating the tomb, this Court called upon the appellant to state as to whether the appellant would be ready to bear the expenses for acquiring the alternate land for the purpose of making deviation in the Highway.

Pursuant thereto,
the appellant made submission before this Court that it was ready to bear the expenses for acquisition of an alternate land for the purpose of making deviation so as not to disturb the existing tomb.

In view of the said submission made by the petitioner-appellant, this Court disposed of the said W.P. No.102746/2021 vide final order dated 25.11.2021 by directing that the tomb in question should be retained in the present place and shall not be disturbed subject to the NC:
2023:KHC-D:10532-DB condition that the appellant would bear the expenses of acquiring any land abutting the tomb for the purpose of widening the road or making deviation.

Subsequently,
respondent No.2, issued a notice dated 14.03.2022 calling upon the appellant to pay a sum of Rs.5,89,000/- for the purpose of paying compensation in favour of respondent No.4-Town Municipal Council, Guledagudda, Bagalkot District, towards road widening and making deviation.

The said notice dated 14.03.2022 was challenged by the appellant before the learned Single Judge in the present W.P. No.101184/2022 which came to be dismissed by holding that appellant had undertaken to bear the expenses and consequently, he was not entitled to challenge the demand notice.
Aggrieved by the impugned order of the learned Single Judge, the appellant is before this Court by way of the present appeal.

3. In the present appeal, the appellant has also filed two applications I.A. No.3/2022 and I.A.

2023:KHC-D:10532-DB

by the appellant, in particular, the communication dated 08.07.2021 issued by respondent No.4-Town Municipal Council, Guledagudda to respondents No.1 to 3 will indicate that the land which was sought to be used/utilized by the respondents No.1 to 3 for the purpose of road widening/deviation without disturbing the existing tomb does not belong to the Town Municipal Council and the question of appellant being fastened with the liability to pay compensation, as demanded in the notice, would not arise.

Further, subsequent to the disposal of the Writ Petition No.101184/2022 vide order 30.03.2022, respondents No.1 to 3 have issued one more notice dated 18.04.2022 calling upon the appellant to pay a total sum of Rs.7,86,495/-.

4. Respondent Nos.1 to 3 have filed their objections to the aforesaid applications inter alia contending that the Town Municipal Council itself has intimated respondents No.1 to 3 that the land sought to be NC: 2023:KHC-D:10532-DB utilized/used for road widening/deviation belong to respondent No.4-Town Municipal Council.

5. In our view, in order to resolve the controversy as to right of respondent No.4 with regard to the land sought to be utilized for the purpose of road widening/deviation, the best person would be respondent No.4-Town Municipal Council, Guledagudda, itself.
However, respondent No.4 though has been served with the notice of this appeal has remained unrepresented and has not appeared before this Court.
It is also relevant to state that the material on record does not disclose any attempt made by respondent No.4-Town Municipal Council to call upon respondents No.1 to 3 to Shri.

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, we deem it just and appropriate to set aside the impugned order and dispose of the appeal by quashing the notices dated 14.03.2022 and 18.04.2022 issued by respondents No.1 to 3 and by reserving liberty in favour of respondents No.1 to 3 to issue fresh notice in the event any demand/claim is made NC: 2023:KHC-D:10532-DB by respondent No.4 against respondents No.1 to 3 and in accordance with law.

6. In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is hereby allowed.
ii) The impugned order dated 30.03.2022 passed in W.P. No.101184/2022 is hereby set aside.
iii) The notices dated 14.03.2022 and 18.04.2022 issued by respondents No.1 to 3 to the appellant are hereby quashed.

iv) Respondents No.1 to 3 are directed to proceed with the widening of the road by way of deviation and without disturbing or obstructing the existing tomb of the sixth pontiff of the appellant-Math and in accordance with law, as expeditiously as possible.

v) Liberty is reserved in favour of respondents No.1 to 3 to issue a fresh notice to the appellant in the event a claim for compensation NC: 2023:KHC-D:10532-DB is made by respondent No.4 against respondents No.1 to 3.
